source.ref: Passaro et al., Boltz-2 (2025); boltz docs/prediction.md

text: Boltz-2's affinity head is a real, documented route to a computed binding value. Verbatim from its docs: affinity_pred_value is log10(IC50) with IC50 in uM, and dG = (6 - y) * 1.364 kcal/mol. The constant 1.364 equals RT*ln(10) at 298.15 K, which is internally consistent with the platform's thermodynamics module.

Boltz confidence_score = 0.8*complex_plddt + 0.2*ptm (ptm for single chains). Verified against our own run to zero floating-point difference: observed 0.8825381994, predicted 0.8825381994. This cross-validates both the retrieved documentation and our parser.

VALIDATION AGAINST MEASURED GROUND TRUTH. Boltz-2 affinity, Huperzine A + human AChE (P22303 mature chain, single-sequence mode): predicted IC50 1274 nM vs ChEMBL measured 5.0 nM — an error of 2.41 log10 units (about 3.3 kcal/mol). The structure itself was confident (ipTM 0.714, complex_plddt 0.930, pTM 0.949) but affinity_probability_binary was only 0.44, i.e. the model was not confident the ligand binds at all. Caveat: run with msa=empty; the docs state single-sequence mode degrades accuracy, so this is a lower bound on achievable performance.

The honest conclusion on computed affinity: a real method with a measured 2.4 log-unit error is scientifically more useful than a fabricated value quoted to 0.1 kcal/mol, because the error is knowable and can be reported. The legacy platform asserted dG to one decimal with no interval; the replacement reports a value together with its validation error against measured data.

Boltz-2 affinity head constraints, verbatim from docs: a single small-molecule ligand chain only, at most 128 heavy+retained-H atoms, not recommended above 56 atoms, protein targets only. It therefore CANNOT be applied to the 25 peptide candidates (3-11 kDa), only to the natural-product warheads. Any peptide affinity must come from a protein-protein method such as PRODIGY instead.
